releases.notes:
# Base Hunting Client 2.4.0 — the command-terminal release

This release adds an **in-game command terminal**: a real command line over the same managers the GUI
and `/bh` use, with argument parsing, Tab completion, history, configurable shortcuts, per-command
permissions and a confirmation step for anything that changes state.

## The command terminal

Enable `command-terminal` and open `/bh gui`; the **Terminal** section is at the bottom of the screen.

- **Nineteen command groups** cover the whole addon: `status`, `modules`, `tasks`, `storage`,
  `navigate`, `baritone`, `kit`, `elytra`, `echest`, `player`, `stash`, `route`, `explore`, `chat`,
  `config`, `database`, `history`, `macro`, `clear`, `gui`.
- **Per-subcommand permissions.** A subcommand can be stricter than its parent — `storage list` is
  read-only, `storage withdraw` is not — and the registry checks the level of the subcommand actually
  being run.
- **Confirmation gate.** A destructive command prints what it is about to do and needs a second Enter;
  any intervening command disarms it.
- **Tab completion** for command names, subcommands and registered argument candidates, routed into
  Meteor's own completion popup.
- **History** with an Up/Down cursor that keeps the half-typed line as a draft, duplicate collapsing
  and a size cap.
- **Shortcuts** (`aliases` setting, `s=status`, `w=withdraw`) and **macros** (`macros` setting,
  `name = step ; step`), replayed through the same registry so permissions still hold.

`/bh terminal run <line>` runs one command from chat and echoes the output; `/bh terminal help` lists
every command.

## Safety

The terminal's input comes from a text box you type into — never from a chat message — so it can offer
the state-changing commands the chat prefix system refuses by default. It has **no shell, no
filesystem access and no arbitrary code execution**: every command is an addon operation, and every
step of a macro goes through the same permission and confirmation checks as a typed command.

## Architecture

| Layer | File | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parser / registry / history / macros | `core/terminal/` | pure, no Minecraft types, headlessly tested |
| Runtime + bindings | `modules/CommandTerminal.java` | builds the registry, binds handlers to the managers |
| GUI | `gui/TerminalRenderer.java`, `gui/BaseHuntingScreen.java` | text box + completion + section |
| Bridge | `commands/BaseHuntCommand.java` | `/bh terminal run <line>` and `/bh terminal help` |

Every handler calls the same public manager method the GUI button and the `/bh` command call, so the
three entry points cannot drift apart.

## Verification

```
./gradlew clean build     # BUILD SUCCESSFUL
./gradlew verifyAddon     # 8 suites, all green
```

| Suite | Assertions |
| --- | --- |
| `plannerTest` | 41 |
| `coreLogicTest` | 147 |
| `baritoneContractTest` | 30 |
| `automationLogicTest` | 196 |
| `hardeningTest` | 21 |
| `storageLogicTest` | 21 |
| `apiContractTest` | 131 |
| `terminalLogicTest` (new) | 86 |

`apiContractTest` now also pins the Meteor GUI members the terminal drives (`GuiTheme.textBox`/`view`,
`WTextBox.action`, `WTextBox.Renderer.getCompletions`, `WView.maxHeight`), so a rename fails the build
instead of the client. Loaded in a real dev client headless (`Initializing Base Hunting Client` →
`(Meteor Client) Loading`, version 2.4.0, no addon errors).

## Asset

`basehunting-2.4.0.jar` — sha256 `5cd44d02e227421be4472a372e50f9de83c313319c220cfb8438b4bcc2612de3`

# Base Hunting Client 2.3.0 — stability hardening

A bug-fix release. Every item below is a real defect found by reading the code, and each has a
regression test that fails if it comes back. No features were removed.

## Flight

- **The v2 autopilot no longer retries a doomed takeoff forever.** `BaseHunterV2` re-asserts "I want to
  fly" every tick, and that call used to reset the launch retry budget, so a takeoff that could never
  succeed was retried indefinitely. The budget now resets only on a genuine off->on transition, a live
  glide replenishes it, and when it is spent the controller reports the failure once and stops. The
  policy lives in a new, pure `DeploymentGovernor` with a headless regression test.
- `BaseHunterV2` re-arms its "not flying" warning after a resumed flight, so every interruption is
  reported, not just the first.

## Memory

- `NewChunks` chunk sets and the `foundAt` timestamp map are now backed by a new `BoundedLongSet`
  (200k cap, oldest-first eviction). A multi-hour flight can no longer grow memory without limit.
- `StashFinder.lastScanned` is size-capped the same way.

## Data

- **`/bh database export` now covers all seven stores.** It previously wrote only four, silently
  dropping the storage registry, storage workflows and kits — restoring such a backup on a fresh
  machine wiped them. A headless test pins the section list so a new store cannot fall out unnoticed.

## Alerts

- `Embed.fingerprint()` now includes the footer and thumbnail, so distinct alerts are no longer
  collapsed by the 3-second dedupe window.
- A webhook dropped on a full queue no longer records its dedupe key, so its retry is not suppressed as
  a duplicate.

## Crashes and correctness

- `ElytraManager.bestSpareRemaining()` guards `mc.player` (was an NPE from `/bh elytra status` before a
  world is joined).
- Task ids come from a single counter, so `cancel(id)` can no longer hit the wrong task.

## Verification

- `./gradlew clean build` is green; the jar is `build/libs/basehunting-2.3.0.jar`.
- `verifyAddon` runs seven headless suites, 0 failures: plannerTest 36, coreLogicTest 196,
  storageLogicTest 131, automationLogicTest 147, hardeningTest 21 (new), apiContractTest 21,
  baritoneContractTest 30.
- The addon loads in a real dev client under Xvfb with no addon exceptions.

## Install

Drop `basehunting-2.3.0.jar` into `.minecraft/mods` alongside Meteor Client and Fabric Loader (Baritone
optional). Requires Minecraft 1.21.11, Fabric, JDK 21.

**SHA-256:** `dceae32676bb343b245ef96cf24e87de625febb9fbc65c7bf21d8bab7b5eb713`

# Base Hunting Client 2.2.0 — the Baritone hardening release

A stability-focused release for the Baritone-powered autopilot (Base Hunter v1). The headline fix is
that a flight that could never start is no longer retried 20 times a second, forever. Baritone
compatibility was rechecked against the real jar and is now locked down by a build-time contract test.

## Fixed

- **Bounded flight deployment (v1).** `BaseHunter` used to call Baritone's elytra path every client tick
  while not gliding, so a doomed takeoff (no firework, blocked launch, spent elytra) was retried
  indefinitely at 20 Hz. It now classifies the player's physical state (`FlightState`) and drives
  launches through a `RetryPolicy`: exponential backoff 1s → 20s, capped at `deploy-retries` attempts
  (default 6), then a single clear report and a clean stop. Swimming or climbing waits without spending
  an attempt; a new leg resets the budget.
- **Baritone health, not just presence.** Baritone bundles its elytra pathfinder as a nested jar; if that
  fails to load, `BaritoneAPI`'s static initialiser throws and every call into it throws too. The helper
  now probes without initialising the class and caches whether the primary baritone actually answers, so
  a half-broken Baritone degrades to "not usable" instead of crashing the addon.
- **One owner of elytra replacement.** v1 set Baritone's `elytraAutoSwap = true`, racing `ElytraManager`
  (the addon's single owner of the chest slot). It is now `false`.

## Added

- **Elytra travel in `NavigationManager`** — long-range navigation can fly instead of only walking.
- **`/bh baritone status | terms | stop`** — see availability, version and flight state; accept Baritone's
  elytra terms; cancel pathing.
- **Baritone HUD line** (optional `show-baritone`).
- **`baritoneContractTest`** — a headless test that reads the real Baritone jar and asserts every member
  the addon drives still exists (30 assertions). Wired into `verifyAddon`, so a Baritone rename fails the
  build instead of failing mid-flight.

## Verification

`./gradlew clean build` is green: 36 + 147 + 30 + 21 + 131 + 184 = **549 headless assertions**. The addon
loads in a real dev client with Baritone present (10 mods, `Path Manager: Baritone`) and no exceptions.

## Install

1. Fabric Loader for Minecraft 1.21.11 + Meteor Client for 1.21.11.
2. Optionally add [Baritone for Meteor](https://meteorclient.com/) — only Base Hunter v1 needs it.
3. Drop `basehunting-2.2.0.jar` into `mods`.

Full guide: [docs/GUIDE.md](https://github.com/logvex-sg/basehuntingclient-baritone/blob/main/docs/GUIDE.md).

# Base Hunting Client 2.1.0 — the automation release

A coordinated automation layer on top of the existing addon. Long-running work is now queued and
serialised by one engine instead of being run inline by disconnected modules, and a reactive brain
lets modules influence each other without calling each other.

**Artifact:** `basehunting-2.1.0.jar` — Minecraft 1.21.11, Fabric, Meteor Client, Java 21.
Baritone stays optional (a `recommends`).

## Highlights

- **One priority task engine.** `AutomationEngine` + `TaskQueue` own every long-running action. Tasks
  run one at a time, are deduplicated by name and category, are re-queued when a failure is retryable,
  and always end in a definite state (completed / partial / failed / cancelled) instead of being
  forgotten. Runners are built lazily from per-category factories.
- **Reactive rules.** `automation-brain` evaluates edge-triggered, cooldown-limited rules over player
  facts (health, hunger, elytra durability, free slots, totems, nearby players, queue depth). Built-in
  reactions replace a failing elytra, pause exploration when the inventory fills or health drops, and
  note player sightings. Rules only call a module's public method or submit a task.
- **Chat commands.** `chat-commands` runs addon commands typed in chat behind a prefix (`!`, `.bh`).
  Only a line the local player typed is ever executed; a message from another player is data and is
  never parsed. Destructive commands are refused unless explicitly allowed.
- **Server kits.** `kit-bot` claims server kits and tracks their cooldowns per server, adopting a
  server-reported cooldown so the client never spams a claim the server will reject.
- **Exact-quantity storage.** `auto-storage` runs withdrawals, deposits and restocks as queued tasks.
  A partial move is a real, verified operation: pick up the source stack, place exactly N, put the
  remainder back — modelled click-for-click in the simulator, so it is checked like any other move.
- **Single owner of travel.** `NavigationManager` is the one place that walks the player to a position.

## New modules

`automation-brain`, `chat-commands`, `kit-bot`, `auto-storage`.

## New commands

`/bh automation status|start|stop|reactions`, `/bh tasks status`, `/bh withdraw <item> [amount]`,
`/bh deposit <item> [amount]`, `/bh kit status|list|claim <name>|all`, `/bh chat run <line>`.

## GUI, HUD and Discord

- The management screen (`/bh gui`) gains an **Automation** section: engine, brain, auto-storage and
  kit status, active and queued task counts, Brain / Storage / Kits toggles, **Claim Kits**,
  **Cancel Tasks** and a recent-reactions view.
- The HUD gains a `show-automation` line (active task, queue depth, kit status).
- `webhook-notifier` gains `notify-tasks` and `notify-chat-commands` categories, with titles, colours
  and per-type cooldowns for the task, kit and chat event types. The asynchronous queue, rate limiting
  and deduplication are unchanged.

## Stability

- A failed-but-retryable task is genuinely re-queued.
- A rule whose condition stays true through its cooldown now fires when the cooldown expires.
- Protected-item matching is namespace-insensitive (`minecraft:elytra` == `elytra`).
- Every task, chat command and kit action reports a real outcome; nothing pretends to succeed.

## Tests

510 headless assertions, all green (`./gradlew clean build`):

| Suite | Assertions | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plannerTest` | 21 | flight-planner maths |
| `coreLogicTest` | 175 | elytra, deployment, scoring, scheduler, bus, recovery |
| `storageLogicTest` | 131 | classification, sorting, transfers, protection, workflows |
| `automationLogicTest` | 147 | tasks, queue, retry/cancel, quantity, chat, kits, rules |
| `apiContractTest` | 36 | Meteor / Minecraft API contract |

The addon loads in a real dev client with no exceptions.

## Docs

`README.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md` (the full manual), `AGENTS.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated for the new

## Base Hunting Client 2.0.0 — the storage release

A complete storage and inventory subsystem on top of the 1.1.0 exploration and equipment release.
Every storage action is planned by pure logic, queued to a single clicker, and only reported as done
once the live container actually matches the planned result.

**Download:** `basehunting-2.0.0.jar` (below). Requires Minecraft 1.21.11, Fabric Loader, and Meteor
Client. Baritone is optional (only Base Hunter v1 needs it).

### New storage modules

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `inventory-manager` | Sorts your inventory into a stable category order — on activate, after closing a container, or on an interval. |
| `chest-sorter` | Sorts any container, deposits/withdraws only the categories you select, and registers opened containers. |
| `storage-network` | A per-server, per-dimension container directory with last-known contents, and travel to a container. |
| `shulker-manager` | Fills, empties, sorts and searches shulker boxes. |
| `restock-manager` | Tops up travel supplies from registered storage, walking there with Baritone when available. |
| `storage-monitor` | Runs named workflows and is the storage status view. |

### Safety first

- **One thing clicks slots: `ContainerInteractionManager`.** Every feature plans moves as pure data and
  submits them there. An operation holds the `INVENTORY` lease for its whole life and only one runs at a
  time, so two features can never click at once.
- **Every operation is verified, not assumed.** The plan is simulated against the live container before
  the first click, and success is reported only once the container actually matches. A wrong settled
  state, a missing slot, or a timeout is a failure with a reason.
- **Deposits only move categories you selected.** A protection list and the reserve settings are a
  second gate; the selected slot, hotbar reserve and protected items never move, and stacks are never
  split.
- **A shulker whose contents were never seen is reported unknown, never empty.**
- **No packets are forged.** The player looks at a block, `interactBlock` runs, items move with normal
  slot clicks. A server refusal is reported, not worked around.

### Also in this release

- Storage & Inventory section in the management screen (`/bh gui`).
- Storage HUD lines (`show-storage`, `show-shulkers`).
- Commands: `/bh storage …`, `/bh shulker …`, `/bh workflow …`, `/bh restock …`.
- Storage notification categories with per-event cooldowns in the Discord notifier.
- A failed operation publishes `CONTAINER_OP_FAILED`, so it shows in chat, the GUI and Discord.

### Verification

`./gradlew clean build` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL. All suites run headlessly via `./gradlew verifyAddon`:

| Suite | Assertions |
| --- | --- |
| `plannerTest` | 21 |
| `coreLogicTest` | 175 |
| `storageLogicTest` | 131 (new) |
| `apiContractTest` | 36 |

The addon also loads in a real dev client: `Initializing Base Hunting Client` → `(Meteor Client) Loading`,
with no addon exceptions.

### Docs

- [README](https://github.com/logvex-sg/basehuntingclient-baritone/blob/main/README.md)
- [Full guide](https://github.com/logvex-sg/basehuntingclient-baritone/blob/main/docs/GUIDE.md)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/logvex-sg/basehuntingclient-baritone/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

### Known limitation

The storage system is verified by headless logic tests and a real client load. It has not been exercised
against a live multiplayer server with real containers. The architecture reports a server refusal as a
failure with a reason rather than a silent false success.
